```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
library(tidyverse)
```

## Overview

This project harvests the course descriptions of Norwegian higher education institutions: every course DBH lists at the institutions with a config, with teacher education as one frame of them (see "Frames"). It takes course codes, years, and semesters as input and produces structured data containing URLs, HTML, and extracted text from course webpages.

**Input:** A dated snapshot of DBH's course list (`dbh_courses()`, see "Input Data") with course metadata (institution, course code, year, semester)

**Output:** The same tibble with added course URL, raw HTML, and extracted text

### Pipeline Stages

| Stage | Code | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Course id `{institution}_{course_code_raw}_{year}_{semester}_{status}` | `add_course_id()` (`R/utils.R`) | `course_id` |
| 2. URL from metadata (institution-specific builders; NA where the URL must be discovered) | `add_course_url()` (`R/add_course_url.R`) | `url` |
| 3. URL discovery (USN, UiT, hivolda, UiO; optional) | `resolve_course_urls()` (`R/resolve_course_urls.R`) | `url`, checkpoint `data/raw/checkpoint/urls_{inst}.RDS` |
| 4. Fetch HTML with checkpointing | `fetch_html_with_checkpoint()` (`R/checkpoint.R`, `R/fetch_html_cols.R`) | `html`, `html_success`, `html_error` |
| 5. Extract text (the page's blocks as text, USN cleanup, PDF text) | `extract_fulltext_from_raw()` (`R/extract_fulltext.R`) | `data/raw/{inst}/{year}/{run}.parquet` (raw harvest) |
| 6. Read each stored page into blocks, per raw partition; the text is the blocks | `partition_blocks()`, `partition_text()` (`R/pipeline.R`) | `extracted_text.RDS` |
| 7. Give each offering its page; anonymize, and deduplicate within each frame | `read_harvest()`, `plan_offerings()`, `frame_plans()` | `course_plans.RDS`, `course_offerings*.RDS` |
| 8. Split each plan into sections | `partition_sections()`, `frame_sections()` | `plan_sections.RDS` |

Stages 1-5 are run per institution by `harvest_institution()`, which dispatches
to a strategy in `R/harvest_strategies.R` (`standard`, `url_discovery`,
`shadow_dom`, `html_pdf_discovery`, `pdf_split`, `json_extract`, `noop`).
`R/institution_config.R` is the single source of truth for each institution:
strategy, the part of the page that holds the plan (`selector`, minus
`exclude`), how a plan's year is known (`plan_years`: `"url"`, `"page"` or
`"current"`), pre/post functions, fetch overrides and the
`section_*` fields. Stages 6-8 and everything after
them are a {targets} pipeline (see "Rebuilding Derived Data").

The raw harvest is append-only Parquet: every harvest adds one file per
institution and DBH year, `data/raw/{inst}/{year}/{run}.parquet`, with what it
fetched, and no raw file is written twice (see "Raw Store and Finalized
Releases"). The steps after it rebuild everything from it with the current
code, so a changed selector or post function needs `targets::tar_make()`, not a
new harvest. A page is read once into blocks (see "Blocks and Sections"), and
both the `extracted_text` and the sections are made from them. The raw store
keeps `extracted_text` only for plans that came from a PDF (uis archive plans,
steiner): that text is the raw data there (uis keeps the PDF too since
2026-10-16).

## Quick Start: Running the Pipeline

The main entry points are in `R/harvest.R`:

```{r}
#| eval: false

# Load all pipeline functions
source("R/utils.R")
source("R/add_course_url.R")
source("R/resolve_course_urls.R")
source("R/fetch_html_cols.R")
source("R/extract_fulltext.R")
source("R/section_heading_map.R")
source("R/blocks.R")
source("R/institution_config.R")
source("R/checkpoint.R")
source("R/harvest_strategies.R")
source("R/harvest.R")

# Harvest a single institution: the rows, not saved (a test)
courses <- dbh_courses("teacher_ed")   # the teacher-ed frame; dbh_courses(): all courses
result <- harvest_institution("hivolda", courses)

# Only one year, or ignore the checkpoints and fetch again
result <- harvest_institution("oslomet", courses, year = 2025)
result <- harvest_institution("ntnu", courses, refetch = TRUE)

# Harvest into the raw store (data/raw/{inst}/{year}/{date}.parquet): all
# institutions, or the given ones; without `courses`, every course of the
# latest DBH snapshot (weeks at the slowest sites)
harvest_all(courses, institutions = "hivolda")
harvest_all()

# Fetch again the offerings without a plan, except pages not found (README
# "Fetch Ledger and Retries"); run targets::tar_make() first
harvest_all(institutions = "uia", year = 2023, retry = TRUE)
```

The source order matters: `R/institution_config.R` refers to functions defined
in `R/fetch_html_cols.R` and `R/extract_fulltext.R`.

### What Happens Under the Hood

1. **`get_institution_config()`**: Looks up strategy, CSS selectors, and overrides
2. **`apply_year_filter()`**: Filters to relevant years based on config
3. **`add_course_id()`**: Creates unique identifiers for each course
4. **`add_course_url()`**: Generates the correct URL for each course
5. **Strategy dispatch**: Routes to the right harvesting strategy (standard, URL discovery, etc.)
6. **`ensure_output_columns()`**: Guarantees uniform output shape

### About Checkpointing

The pipeline uses **checkpointing** to avoid re-downloading data. If the script stops or crashes,
or a site refuses the harvest (HTTP 403 or 429; see "Fetch Ledger and Retries"):

- Already-downloaded HTML is saved in `data/raw/checkpoint/html_{institution}.RDS` (`course_id`, `html`, `html_success`, `html_error`)
- Re-running the script fetches only courses not in the checkpoint (anti-join by `course_id`)
- This saves time and is polite to institutional servers

The checkpoint only resumes an interrupted harvest; it is a cache, not the
record. Offerings already in a raw file are skipped by `harvest_all()` itself
(see "Raw Store and Finalized Releases"). For "page" and "current" sites
(`plan_years`) the checkpoint is removed before every harvest, because their
pages change over time and an old copy must not stand in for a new one.

### Rebuilding Derived Data

Everything after the harvest is a {targets} pipeline: `_targets.R` lists the
steps, `R/pipeline.R` holds their functions. Run it after a harvest or after
changing code or config:

```{r}
#| eval: false
targets::tar_make()               # rebuild whatever is outdated
targets::tar_outdated()           # what would be rebuilt, without building
targets::tar_read(metrics_check)  # changes against the metrics snapshot
targets::tar_read(unmapped)       # headings the section extractor could not map
targets::tar_read(heading_use)    # pages per heading-map pattern (0 = unused)
targets::tar_read(privacy_check)  # personal data found in data/processed/
targets::tar_read(frozen_check)   # changes to the finalized release (empty before one)
targets::tar_read(gaps)           # course-years without a plan, and why
targets::tar_read(coverage)       # every offering of each frame: fetch outcome, plan, retry
targets::tar_read(changed_pages)  # pages whose text changed between harvest runs
```

{targets} keeps each step's result in `_targets/` (gitignored) together with a
hash of its inputs and of the code it calls, and reruns a step only when one of
those changed. The steps that read pages run once per raw partition, an
institution's DBH year (`data/raw/{inst}/{year}/`, `raw_partitions()`), so no
step holds more than one partition's HTML: `blocks` (every stored page read
once), `page_text` (its text, anonymized plan and plan id), `page_headings`
(for `unmapped` and `heading_use`) and `source_sections` (the sections of the
pages plans are cut from). A new raw file of uib 2025, or a change to uib's
entry in `R/institution_config.R`, rebuilds only uib's partitions, while a
change to shared code (`R/anonymize.R`, `R/section_heading_map.R`,
`R/extract_sections.R`) reruns that step for every partition. Which page each
offering takes can cross years (a spring offering reads the academic year's
page, a current site's snapshot serves every year), so that is decided per
institution without reading the pages (`pages`: `read_harvest(content =
FALSE)`, which puts the page id, `{inst}/{year}/{run}/{row}`, in place of the
page), and the steps over all offerings (`courses`, `plans`, `sections`,
`offerings`) join the partitions' results by page id. The pipeline writes the
data files of each frame (see "Frames") in `data/interim/` and
`data/processed/` (see "Data Files: Published and Internal"),
`app/course_browser/data/browser_data.RDS`, the OJS Parquet files,
`data/data_notes.md` and `methods.md`. The harvest is not part of it.

`methods.md` (from `methods.qmd`) holds the choices behind the data that an
article's methods section must report, by topic, with numbers computed from the
data; a decision that changes what the data mean gets an entry there.
`data/interim/plan_gaps.RDS` (target `gaps`) lists every course-year without a
plan with the reason (no URL, 404, fetch error, page but no plan) and flags
the gaps between two years with plans, the ones worth checking by hand; the
data notes summarize it ("Course-years without a plan").

The steps run on 4 local worker processes ({crew}, set in `tar_option_set()`
in `_targets.R`), several partitions at a time. A full build takes about 21
minutes, a build with nothing to do about 10 seconds (2026-10-16). To debug a step with `browser()`, run in the current session instead:
`targets::tar_make(callr_function = NULL, use_crew = FALSE)`.

The pipeline ends by comparing the built data of each frame with a snapshot of
per-institution and per-section counts and median text lengths
(`R/pipeline_metrics.R`, `tests/snapshots/pipeline_metrics_{frame}.csv`).
Changes beyond tolerance show as a warning in `tar_make()` (target
`metrics_check`, with the frame) and make
`tests/testthat/test-pipeline-metrics.R` fail. The teacher-ed snapshot stays
put; the all-courses one changes with each harvest. When a change is intended,
update the snapshot of the frames it changed and commit it together with the
change:

```{r}
#| eval: false
source("R/utils.R"); source("R/pipeline_metrics.R")
check_pipeline_metrics(update = TRUE, frames = "all")
```

### Frames

The pipeline builds every offering in the raw store, and writes the data files
of two frames (`FRAMES`): `all`, every harvested offering, in `data/interim/`
and `data/processed/`; and `teacher_ed`, the offerings in the teacher-ed frame
of the latest DBH snapshot (`dbh_courses("teacher_ed")`, matched on the
offering without its status, `frame_members()`), in the `teacher_ed/` folders
of both (`frame_dir()`). The text, plan id and sections of a page are the same
in both; the plans are deduplicated within each frame (`frame_plans()`), so a
teacher-ed plan has the years, text and sections of its own earliest
teacher-ed offering, whatever else the raw store holds, and a harvest of other
courses leaves the teacher-ed files as they were. The teacher-ed files are the
releases' (`finalize_release()`, `release_data()`, target `frozen_check`), the
browsers' and `methods.md`'s; the data notes, the gaps and the audits read
those of all courses. Each frame has its metrics snapshot, and target
`coverage` its DBH offerings.

Per-institution prose notes are edited directly in `data/data_notes.qmd`.

### Packages and Tests

Package versions are pinned with renv: `renv.lock` records R 4.6.1 and every
package the code uses, and R started in this folder loads them from the
project library in `renv/` (activated by `.Rprofile`). On a new machine,
`renv::restore()` installs them. Harvesting USN also needs Chrome or Chromium
on the machine, which chromote drives. After adding a package, record it with
`renv::snapshot()` and commit `renv.lock`.

The tests run with `testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat")`, and on GitHub
Actions for every push and pull request to main
(`.github/workflows/tests.yml`, packages from `renv.lock`). Tests that need
the harvested or built data (only `data/input/` is in git), a browser or external URLs
skip themselves there.

## The Yearly Harvest

A new year is harvested with the same code as the first harvest:
`harvest_all()` fetches only the offerings no raw file holds, and
`tar_make()` rebuilds everything from the raw store. Each year, in this order:

1. **September-November: the sites that show only the current plan.** UiO,
   MF, NMBU and Steiner replace a plan when the next academic year begins, so
   a year without a harvest has no plans for them (see "Sites that show only
   the current plan"). Harvest them in every academic year, whether or not
   DBH has a new year:

   ```r
   harvest_all(institutions = c("uio", "mf", "nmbu", "steiner"))
   ```

   This fetches again the pages of every course of the latest DBH year in
   the snapshot. Samas has `plan_years = "current"` too, but fetches nothing
   (`noop`).

2. **When DBH has the new year: a new DBH snapshot.** DBH has the year when
   this query returns rows (Semester 1 is spring, 3 autumn); until then it
   fails with DBH's empty answer:

   ```r
   rdbhapi::dbh_data(208, filters = list("Årstall" = "2026"), variables = "Semester") |>
     dplyr::count(Semester)
   ```

   Then, from the repository root, `Rscript data-raw/courses.R` writes
   `data/input/dbh_courses_{date}.parquet` and
   `dbh_programmes_{date}.parquet` (DBH's whole tables 208 and 347; the
   download of table 208 is about 700 MB). Commit both. From then on
   `dbh_courses()` and the pipeline read the new snapshot: the teacher-ed
   frame and target `coverage` follow it, and an offering already harvested
   keeps its `course_id` (see "Input Data").

3. **Harvest.** `harvest_all()` fetches every offering of the snapshot that
   no raw file holds: the new year, and rows DBH added to earlier years since
   the last snapshot. `harvest_all(year = 2026)` fetches the new year only.
   A site that shows only the current plan gets another snapshot, now with
   the new year's courses. At the slowest sites this takes days, so run
   institutions side by side (below). Raw files exist only on this machine:
   back up `data/raw/` once the harvest is done.

4. **Rebuild and check.** Run `targets::tar_make()` and read the targets of
   "Rebuilding Derived Data":
   - `metrics_check`: the all-courses frame changes with every harvest, the
     teacher-ed frame with a new year. Explain the rows in the commit and
     update the snapshots of those frames
     (`check_pipeline_metrics(update = TRUE, frames = ...)`).
   - `frozen_check`: the plans of a new year are not listed. A row (an
     offering that left the teacher-ed frame in the new snapshot, a plan a
     site reworded) is a change to the last release; explain it in the
     commit.
   - `privacy_check`: must have no rows.
   - `unmapped` and `heading_use`: headings of new or changed page layouts.
   - `coverage` of the new year by institution, and `changed_pages`.

   Then fetch again the pages that gave no plan (a 404 is not tried again;
   see "Fetch Ledger and Retries") and rebuild:

   ```r
   harvest_all(year = 2026, retry = TRUE)
   targets::tar_make()
   ```

   Update `methods.qmd` where it names the snapshot, the years or the harvest
   dates ("Population and sampling frame", "Harvest"), and
   `data/data_notes.qmd` where a site changed.

5. **Audit.** In Claude Code, `/audit-institutions fulltext`, then
   `sections` and `anonymization` (see "Auditing a Pipeline Step"), for all
   institutions or those whose site changed. The skill has no year option:
   its packets sample each institution's courses of all years. A finding is
   fixed in the config or the heading map and rebuilt with `tar_make()`,
   without a new harvest.

6. **Release.** Tag the commit and finalize the release (see "Raw Store and
   Finalized Releases"):

   ```r
   # after git tag data-YYYY-MM-DD
   source("R/utils.R"); source("R/release.R")
   finalize_release("data-YYYY-MM-DD")   # then commit tests/snapshots/raw_manifest.csv
   ```

   The hand-over to the coding project, `release_data("data-YYYY-MM-DD")`
   (into `../TEPS_course_content_coding/data`), is the project lead's
   decision and step, because the coders work from that repository.

### Several Institutions at Once

`harvest_all()` takes the institutions one after another. At the slowest sites
a harvest of every course takes days (NTNU and UiB ask for 10 seconds between
requests in robots.txt), so run several institutions side by side, each in
its own R process, with the institution or institutions it harvests in
`institutions`. From the repository root, with a log per process:

```sh
mkdir -p tmp/harvest_logs
for inst in ntnu uib uio; do
  nohup Rscript -e "for (f in c('R/utils.R', 'R/add_course_url.R', 'R/resolve_course_urls.R',
    'R/fetch_html_cols.R', 'R/extract_fulltext.R', 'R/section_heading_map.R', 'R/blocks.R',
    'R/institution_config.R', 'R/checkpoint.R', 'R/harvest_strategies.R', 'R/harvest.R')) source(f)
    harvest_all(institutions = '$inst')" > tmp/harvest_logs/${inst}_$(date +%F).log 2>&1 &
done
pgrep -af harvest_all   # the harvests still running
```

- **One process per institution.** Each institution has its own checkpoint
  (`data/raw/checkpoint/*_{inst}.RDS`), raw folder, run names and ledger, so
  processes for different institutions do not collide. Never harvest one
  institution in two processes at once: they would share its checkpoint, and
  the build stops at an offering in two runs.
- **One process per host.** A process pauses between its own requests (3-5
  seconds, or the institution's `request_delay`), so two processes on one
  host double the load on it. Institutions on a shared host (a common course
  catalogue) go in one process, `institutions = c(...)`, which harvests them
  one after another. Each configured institution has a host of its own
  today. Read the robots.txt of a new site before its first harvest: a
  `Crawl-delay` goes in `request_delay`.
- **At night.** Start long harvests in the evening, so that most requests
  come outside the sites' busy hours. A site with the year in the URL can be
  stopped (end the process) and started again: the checkpoint, saved every
  50 pages, resumes it. A "page" or "current" site fetches all its pages
  again at every start, so let it run to the end. A site that answers 403 or
  429 stops its own harvest; start it again later.
- **Memory and the build.** A process keeps its institution's pages in memory
  until it writes the run, so check free memory before starting more of them.
  `tar_make()` (4 workers) builds the runs written so far; run it when the
  harvests are done, or audit only the institutions whose harvest has ended.

## Adding a New Institution

To add support for a new institution, you need to modify **two files**. In
Claude Code, the `/add-institution` skill walks through the same steps.

### 1. Add config entry to `R/institution_config.R`

```{r}
#| eval: false

# Add to the institution_configs list:
newuni = list(
  code = "1234",                  # DBH code; several if it changed: c("0264", "1177")
  strategy = "standard",          # or url_discovery, shadow_dom, etc.
  selector = ".main-content",     # the element that holds the course plan
  exclude = ".contact",           # optional: parts of it that are not the plan
  plan_years = "url",             # year in the URL; "page" or "current": see R/institution_config.R
  # url_year = "academic",        # if the URL's year is the academic year (ntnu, hvl, oslomet, uis)
  section_strategy = "html"       # how the plan is split; see "Blocks and Sections"
)
```

**How to find CSS selectors:**

1. Open a course page in your browser
2. Right-click on the course description text → "Inspect"
3. Look for a `class` or `id` attribute that wraps the content
4. Use the SelectorGadget tool: https://rvest.tidyverse.org/articles/selectorgadget.html
5. Test your selector to make sure it captures all course text

`selector` names one element (the first match is used); choose the
narrowest element that holds the whole plan with its title and facts box
(`course_plan_spec.md`), and leave out navigation, contact boxes (staff
names) and widgets inside it with `exclude` (hvl, nord, uib, uio, uis, mf,
hivolda do this). Name the title and facts box in `facts`, so that they stay
out of the sections and the plan id.

### 2. Add URL builder to `R/add_course_url.R`

Add a case to `case_match()` and create a URL-building function:

```{r}
#| eval: false

# In add_course_url(), add:
"newuni" ~ add_course_url_newuni(course_code, year, semester_name),

# Create a helper function for your institution
add_course_url_newuni <- function(course_code, year, semester) {
  semester <- case_match(semester, "Vår" ~ "spring", "Høst" ~ "autumn")
  glue::glue("https://www.newuni.no/courses/{year}/{semester}/{tolower(course_code)}")
}
```

### 3. Test Your Changes

```{r}
#| eval: false

# Load pipeline and test
courses <- dbh_courses()   # every DBH course; the institution's code must be in its config
result <- harvest_institution("newuni", courses, year = 2025)

# Inspect results
result |> select(course_code, url, html_success, extracted_text) |> head()
result$extracted_text[1]  # Inspect first result
```

Expand a little bit at a time, for example by year. Add more years as the pipeline works.

For standard institutions no changes to `R/extract_fulltext.R` or
`R/harvest_strategies.R` are needed. Sites that need a browser (Shadow DOM),
PDF splitting or URL discovery need a strategy function in
`R/harvest_strategies.R`.

## Post-Harvest: Anonymization and Deduplication

The pipeline anonymizes and deduplicates the course plans in three stages:

1. **Anonymize** (`anonymize_text()`): Removes PII (teacher names, emails, phone numbers, staff lists "Name (Role)", signature lines "Name, dekan"), dates, seasons, and administrative year references ("Opprettet 2020", "2023/2024") from `extracted_text`, producing a readable `course_plan` column. Content years (e.g., "etter 1945", "NOU 2015:2") are preserved. Institution-specific handlers (`.anon_*()`) run first, then the generic cleanup (`.anon_generic()`).
2. **Normalize** (`normalize_plan_text()`): Applies lossy transforms (lowercasing, heading synonyms, blanket year removal, whitespace squishing) on `course_plan` for content hashing
3. **Deduplicate** (`plan_ids()`, `plan_table()`): Groups identical normalized texts under a shared `plan_content_id`, within each frame (see "Frames")

**Output columns:**

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `course_plan` | Anonymized, readable text (primary column for consumers) |
| `extracted_text` | Raw extracted text (kept for debugging) |
| `course_plan_normalized` | Lossy normalized text (internal, for hashing) |
| `plan_content_id` | SHA-256 hash of `course_plan_normalized` |
| `plan_year_basis` | How the plan's year is known: `url`, `page` or `current` (`plan_years` in the config) |
| `harvested_at` | For `current` sites: the date of the harvest the page comes from |

A page with no section to read and under 1,500 characters is a page shell,
not a plan (`SHELL_MAX_NCHAR`): its offerings keep their text but get no
`plan_content_id`.

### Sites that show only the current plan

UiO, MF, NMBU and Steiner (`plan_years = "current"`) publish only the plan in
force, without a year in the URL. A harvest therefore holds the plans of the
academic year (August-July) it was made in, and a later harvest cannot recover
them. Their raw files are snapshots:

- Each harvest of such a site fetches the pages of its latest DBH year again
  and adds them as a dated raw file, stamped `harvested_at`. Checkpoints from
  an earlier academic year are removed first (they would return last year's
  pages), and a harvest in June-August warns (the site may already show next
  year's plan).
- `read_harvest()` gives each offering the page of its course code from the
  latest harvest in the offering's academic year (autumn Y: Y/Y+1, spring Y:
  Y-1/Y), or no page. A page counts for its course and year whichever DBH row
  it was fetched for, so DBH rows published years later still find it.
- So harvest these sites once in every academic year (best September-November
  or February-April), whether or not DBH has a new year; a year without a
  harvest has no plans for them.

Their runs are `2026-04-04` (the user's earlier harvest, 2025/26) and
`2026-09-30` (2026/27), both of DBH 2025 rows (`data/raw/{inst}/2025/`). A
harvest date comes from the `harvested_at` column or the run's name, never
from a file's modification time, which a copy changes. The rest of the April
backup, for sites with the year in the URL, is in `data/backup/2026-04-04/` and
is not read. Raw files exist only locally: back them up.

A "page" site (NLA) and a "current" site change their pages over time, so
their checkpoints are removed before every harvest and all pages are fetched
again; for "url" sites the checkpoint only resumes an interrupted harvest.

### Raw Store and Finalized Releases

The raw store is Parquet (zstd), one file per institution, DBH year (`year`)
and harvest run: `data/raw/{inst}/{year}/{run}.parquet`. A run is named by its
date, a second run of an institution the same day by date and time
(`{date}_{HHMMSS}`, which sorts after it), so a retry need not wait for the
next day. No raw file is written twice. A harvest fetches only the offerings no
raw file holds yet (a current site: a new snapshot) and `harvest_all()` saves
them as a new run (`write_raw_run()`), with the run's fetch ledger (see "Fetch
Ledger and Retries"). `harvest_all(year = 2026)` and
`harvest_all()` therefore both just add what is new. An offering is matched on
institution, code, year and semester: when a new DBH snapshot changes its
status, it keeps the `course_id` it was first harvested under.
`read_harvest()` combines the runs; an offering in two runs stops the build.

A raw file holds the rows as the harvest returned them: the offering's DBH
columns as they were at the harvest (under DBH's names until 2026-10-16,
which `read_raw()` renames: `dbh_rename()`, see "Variables"), `url`, `html`,
`html_success`, `html_error` (the error message), `harvested_at`, `retry` (a
retry run) and `harvest_row`, the row's place in its run, so `read_raw()`
gives the rows in the order they were harvested (which offering a plan's text
comes from depends on it). `extracted_text` is kept only for a row without `html`, text read from
a PDF, the raw data there; uis keeps the PDF's bytes too (`pdf`, since
2026-10-16). Elsewhere `tar_make()` rebuilds the text from `html`.

The format changed once, on 2026-10-16; the content did not. The RDS raw
files of the harvests before (`data/raw/html_{inst}.RDS`, the first harvests,
and `data/raw/harvests/{date}/html_{inst}.RDS`) were written one to one to the
Parquet store by `data-raw/raw_to_parquet.R`, which compares every run with its
RDS file column by column and row by row, and `tar_make()` then rebuilt release
data-2026-10-16 exactly. The first harvests did not stamp `harvested_at` and
were not dated: their run is named by the day their RDS file was written
(2026-09-30 to 2026-10-06), and their `harvested_at` stays empty. The RDS files
are no longer read; they stay in `data/raw/` until they are removed by hand,
after a backup.

A page that gave no plan can be fetched again with `harvest_all(retry = TRUE)`
(see "Fetch Ledger and Retries"). Retry before finalizing a release;
afterwards it changes the release.

To finalize a release, after `tar_make()` and tagging the commit:

```r
source("R/utils.R"); source("R/release.R")
finalize_release("data-YYYY-MM-DD")   # then commit tests/snapshots/raw_manifest.csv
release_data("data-YYYY-MM-DD")       # hand-over to the coding project
```

`finalize_release()` makes every raw file and fetch ledger read-only (an overwrite then fails),
lists them with md5 sums in `tests/snapshots/raw_manifest.csv`, and keeps the
release's offerings, plans and sections (the teacher-ed frame's, see
"Frames") in `data/releases/{tag}/`. On every
build `tar_read(frozen_check)` lists any change to the release: a raw file
changed or missing, an offering gone or linked to another plan, a plan gone or
with other text, a section changed. Plans
added later (a new DBH year) are not changes. A planned change to the release
(a privacy fix, a section fix after the coders' check) means a new release:
finalize it, and `release_data()` writes the old -> new `plan_content_id`
crosswalk. Until then `frozen_check` lists the planned changes on every build,
and a change nobody intended would be listed among them, so each commit
explains the rows it adds, and the next release follows soon after the fixes.
A section fix keeps the plan's id, so the crosswalk does not show it;
`release_data()` lists such sections (plan, section, changed, added or
removed) in `sections_changed.csv`.

**Output files** (of all courses; the teacher-ed frame's in the `teacher_ed/` folders, see "Frames"):

- `data/processed/course_offerings.RDS` — published slim dataset: course rows with DBH metadata + `plan_content_id` FK (no url, no text)
- `data/interim/course_offerings_full.RDS` — internal working file: same rows plus `url`, `extracted_text`, `course_plan`, `course_plan_normalized`; the teacher-ed one is used by the course_browser app
- `data/processed/course_plans.RDS` — one row per unique plan per course code per institution, with the offering its text comes from (`source_course_id`)

### Fetch Ledger and Retries

Every harvest run also writes its fetch ledger,
`data/raw/{inst}/ledger/{run}.parquet`: one row per offering of the run, in
the run's order, with how its page was fetched (`fetch_ledger()`):

| Column | Holds |
|---|---|
| `run`, `institution`, `course_id`, `url` | the run, the offering and the URL requested |
| `requested_at` | when the request was sent |
| `http_status` | the answer's HTTP status, also of a site's own not-found page |
| `outcome` | the outcome class, below |
| `bytes`, `sha256` | size and SHA-256 of the page as stored (`html`, else the text read from a PDF) |
| `raw_file` | the raw file that holds the row |
| `dbh_snapshot` | the date of the DBH snapshot the harvest's offerings came from (`dbh_courses()`) |

The outcome classes (`fetch_outcome()`): `ok` (a page or a PDF's text was
stored); `not_found` (HTTP 404 or 410; HTTP 400, UiB's answer for a semester
before its first; or the site's own not-found page, HVL's "Course not
found"); `shell` (the site answers that it has nothing for that year, NTNU's
"No course information available for this academic year"); `server_error`
(HTTP 5xx); `timeout` (no answer: a timeout or a failed connection);
`blocked` (HTTP 403 or 429); `error` (anything else); `no_url` (no URL to
request: the URL builder or the URL discovery found none).

The ledger is raw data like its run: append-only, written only by
`harvest_all()`, locked by `finalize_release()`. It holds URLs and hashes, no
page text. It records the page requests (`fetch_html_cols()`, UiS's PDFs);
USN's pages rendered in Chrome, Steiner's subject PDFs and the requests of URL
discovery have no status or time in it. The runs before 2026-10-16 have no
ledger: `raw_ledger()` reconstructs theirs from the raw rows, without
`requested_at` and `dbh_snapshot`, and with `http_status` only where the
error message gives it ("HTTP 404 Not Found."); their `recorded` is `FALSE`.
Target `ledger` is the ledger of all runs, recorded or reconstructed.

**Retries within a harvest** (`site_request()`): a request without an answer
(a timeout, a failed connection) or with HTTP 500, 502, 503 or 504 is tried
again, 3 times in all, after 30 and then 60 seconds; any other answer is
final. A site that answers 403 or 429 refuses the harvest: its harvest stops,
the pages fetched so far stay in the checkpoint (the next harvest resumes
there), and `harvest_all()` goes on with the next institution.

**Retries between harvests:** `harvest_all(retry = TRUE)` fetches again the
offerings that have no plan in the current build
(`data/interim/course_offerings_full.RDS`, so run `tar_make()` first), past
the checkpoint, by how the URL the build gives them answered last, for
whichever offering it was requested (`offering_outcome()`): every outcome but
`not_found`, so a page not found is not asked for again, and always a URL
nobody has requested (a spring offering's academic-year page). `retry` can
name the classes instead: `retry = c("timeout", "server_error")` only failed
fetches, `retry = "not_found"` pages that may have been published since. The
retried offerings are saved as a new run, marked `retry`, and `read_harvest()`
gives a retried offering its latest row with a page. A site that shows only
the current plan is not retried; it takes a new snapshot in each academic
year.

```{r}
#| eval: false
harvest_all(institutions = "uia", year = 2023, retry = TRUE)
harvest_all(institutions = "uib", retry = "server_error")
```

**Coverage and changed pages.** Target `coverage` lists every offering of
each frame of the latest DBH snapshot (`frame`: `all`, every course at the
institutions with a config, or `teacher_ed`) with `outcome` (how its URL
answered last; `not requested`, or `not harvested`: in no raw run),
`has_plan` (in that frame's files), and `retry` (no plan, and
`harvest_all(retry = TRUE)` would fetch it again): the coverage report of a
release. Target `changed_pages` lists the
pages whose plan text changed between two runs that fetched the same URL (a
site that reworded an old page; a current site's plan of a new year). The
body's `sha256` alone cannot tell, since some sites change the body on every
fetch (Liferay's `authToken` at NTNU and OsloMet), so where the bodies differ
the text the pipeline reads from them is compared.

```{r}
#| eval: false
targets::tar_read(coverage) |> dplyr::filter(frame == "teacher_ed") |>
  dplyr::count(institution, outcome, has_plan, retry)
targets::tar_read(changed_pages)
```

## Post-Harvest: Section Extraction

The pipeline splits each course plan into its parts and writes
`data/processed/plan_sections.RDS` with one row per plan and section
(`plan_content_id`, `institution`, `course_code`, `source_course_id`, `section`,
`text`), keyed like `course_plans.RDS`. A plan's sections are cut from the page
of `source_course_id`, the offering whose text the plan keeps, so they match
its `course_plan`. The seven sections are
`course_content`, `learning_outcomes`, `teaching_methods`, `assessment`,
`coursework_requirements`, `prerequisites` and `reading_list`. Section text is
anonymized with the same `anonymize_text()` as `course_plan`: sections are cut
from the raw `html`/`extracted_text`, so this step must keep anonymizing.
Admission text, exam logistics and placeholder rows such as "Se fagplanen." are
left out. What a section holds and what it leaves out is set by
`course_plan_spec.md`.

`tar_read(metrics)` has the number of plans with each section per
institution and `pct_text_in_sections`, the median share of a plan's text
that its sections hold (what is left is metadata, admission text, exam
logistics and headings the map does not know). `tar_read(unmapped)` lists the
headings the extractor could not map, with the number of pages each is on,
and `tar_read(heading_use)` every pattern of the heading map with the pages
it opens a section on: a pattern on no page is a candidate for removal (the
html reader's text fallback, used for uis PDF plans, is not counted). To map a new heading, add a pattern to
`R/section_heading_map.R`; how each institution is split is set by the
`section_*` fields in `R/institution_config.R`.

### Blocks and Sections

Each page is read once into a **block table** (`R/blocks.R`): one row per
heading, sub-heading or piece of text, in document order, with the section a
heading maps to. `sectionize()` (`R/extract_sections.R`) then walks the blocks
with the same rules for every institution: a heading opens its section (an
unmapped one closes it), a sub-heading switches section only inside a mapped
one, and text goes to the open section. What differs between institutions is
how their pages are read, set by `section_strategy` and the other `section_*`
fields in `R/institution_config.R`:

| `section_strategy` | Institutions | Reads |
|---|---|---|
| `html` | oslomet, uia, ntnu, inn, hiof, hivolda, hvl, mf, nord, nih, uib, uio, uis, uit, nmbu | The DOM under `selector`. Falls back to `text` when it finds < 3 sections, if the text gives more sections and one that no heading on the page names |
| `json` | nla | Titles and contents in the embedded EmneplanPage JSON |
| `text` | usn, steiner (+ the fallback, e.g. uis PDF plans) | Heading-shaped lines in `extracted_text`; skips the title and facts box and a table of contents ("Innholdsfortegnelse", usn), and a line repeating one of its entries is a heading, so an unmapped one ("Annet") ends the section; inside a reading list opened by a whole heading only a whole heading switches section (book titles) |
| `noop` | samas | — |

The `html` reader writes a table as one line per row, its cells separated by
tabs, so an exam table has one line per exam.

Fields for the `html` reader:

- `selector` and `exclude` (shared with the fulltext): the container, and
  elements in it that are not read (mf's contact card, banner and the facts
  box's buttons; uis's facts-box links; nord's "Kopier lenke" label; ntnu's timetable tab and the exam tab's
  link, rooms and comments). `exclude` holds CSS selectors; an entry that
  starts with "/" is XPath, for an element picked by its text (ntnu's
  "Dato", "Tid" and "Sted og rom" labels with the value after them).
- `facts` (shared with the fulltext): the elements that hold the title, the
  course code and the facts box (every `html` institution; for nla's JSON
  the parts `"title"` and `"table"`), and plan text in no section that
  changes from year to year while the plan stays the same (ntnu's admission
  programme list, credit-reduction box and subject areas; uia's student
  evaluation and admission flags; hivolda's evaluation and examiner
  sentences and programme list; nord's "Type emne"). Their blocks are flagged `facts`: in
  `course_plan`, but in no section (a heading inside them opens none), and
  not in the plan text (`plan_text` in the fulltext table) that the plan id,
  the shell rule and the sections' text fallback read, so a campus or
  programme list that changes from year to year does not split a plan. In
  pages read as text (usn, steiner, uis PDF plans) the title and facts box
  are the lines before the plan: a metadata block matching
  `section_text_header`, or the lines before a table of contents (usn).
- `section_heading_selector`: section headings (default `h2`; ntnu
  `"h2, h3:not(.exam-assessment-form)"`, inn's `div.label`, uib's and mf's
  `summary`, nord's `button.ac-trigger`).
- `section_scope`: elements that hold a section of their own (`details`,
  nord's `div.ac`); the section open around them continues after them.
- `section_initial`: section for text before the first heading (mf's untitled
  intro is course_content).
- `section_untitled`: elements that hold a section without a heading, as
  `c(selector = section)` (nord's short description `div.placeholder-text`
  is course_content; the title and course code before it stay out).
- `section_fields`: hivolda's Drupal fields (`div.field-<name>`) are the
  headings, each mapped to a section by its class name; text outside the
  fields (title, programmes) is in the fulltext but in no section.
- `section_subheading_selector`: elements inside a section that switch to
  another section (uio `"h3, h4, p"`; `"p"` for uia, oslomet, hiof, hvl, nmbu;
  mf's intro paragraphs). A `<p>` counts if its whole text (minus a trailing
  colon) equals a heading pattern, or if its leading `<em>`/`<strong>` run or
  its first or last `<br>`-separated line does (uia `<p><em>Faget i
  praksis</em>I løpet …</p>`). A whole-bold `<p>` that names no section is a
  group label: it ends a sub-section and returns to the parent. Sub-headings
  act only under a mapped heading (oslomet's programme "Fagplan" block stays
  out); one naming the section already open ("Kunnskap") stays as content. A
  `<p>` in a list item is skipped unless that `<li>` holds a section heading
  (oslomet's accordion). An unmapped `h3` ("Karakterskala") hands its text
  back to the parent section, keeping the heading as its first line. A
  colon-ended lead-in naming a coursework gate ("… følgende obligatoriske
  aktiviteter:") starts coursework_requirements.

Other fields:

- `section_text_header`: regex for a title + metadata block at the top of
  `extracted_text` (uis PDFs: "Emnekode:", "Tilbys av:"; steiner's PDFs:
  "Studiepoeng", "Undervisningsspråk"); the `text` reader skips it and files
  the untitled paragraph after it as course_content, and the plan id leaves
  it out.
- `section_inline_coursework`: move "Arbeidskrav (AK): …" / "Obligatorisk
  deltakelse …" lines from assessment to coursework_requirements (nord).
- `exam_sessions`: the page lists the exam parts once per exam session
  (ntnu's exam tab: "Ordinær eksamen - Høst 2022", "Utsatt eksamen - …").
  The assessment section and the plan id keep the parts of one session, the
  first ordinary one, without the session headings and the exam system
  (`.exam_tab_design()`); `course_plan` keeps them all.
- `section_pointer`: a section whose text is only a pointer to another block
  of the page ("Se fagplanen.") takes the text under a sub-heading of that
  block, after a lead naming the source. oslomet: teaching methods from the
  subject's "Fagplan" block ("Fagets arbeids- og undervisningsformer"), as
  "Se fagplanen. Fagplanen sier: …". The parts under the `append`
  sub-headings join their section when the page has it with text of its own
  (oslomet: the Fagplan's "Arbeidskrav" and attendance parts join the
  coursework requirements), and a line starting with a `stop` label ends a
  part (labels the page did not mark as sub-headings: "Skikkethetsvurdering",
  "Vurderingsuttrykk").

### Heading Map and Cleanup

`match_heading_to_section()` (`R/section_heading_map.R`) checks exact equality
against every pattern first, then substring patterns in table order (first hit
wins; rows with `exact = TRUE` only match whole headings). The `text` reader
passes `word_start = TRUE` so "elevkunnskap" does not match "kunnskap", and only
accepts heading-shaped lines (capitalised, ≤ 8 words, no digits, no "Label:
value", no closing full stop). Patterns mapped to `".drop"` end the current
section and their text is discarded: admission headings ("Opptak til emnet",
"Opptakskrav", "Hvem kan ta dette emnet?") and exam logistics ("Mer om eksamen
ved UiO", "Sensorordning", resit headings such as "Ny/utsatt eksamen"). Exam
aids, exam language and grading scale stay in assessment. A `label` heading
("Hjelpemidler til eksamen", "Eksamensspråk", "Fravær fra obligatorisk
aktivitet") stays as a line of its section, since the text under it ("Ingen",
"Norsk.") says nothing alone; with nothing but a dash or pointer under it, it
goes.

HTML is parsed by `.read_doc()`, which drops `script`, `style`, `select` and
`label` (ntnu script text, uib semester picker); the `json` reader parses the
page itself because its data is in a `<script>`.

A prerequisites label inside course_content ("Forkunnskapskrav", uit's "Om
emnet") moves the paragraph it names to prerequisites
(`.split_inline_prerequisites()`), and a paragraph of 40 or more characters
that its section repeats is kept once.

`.clean_sections()` removes `.drop` rows, strips page widgets, pointers and
stock logistics sentences from assessment/coursework (`.section_noise`: uib
banner and footer, hvl's "Mer om hjelpemidler" link, oslomet's resit
sentence, …; notices about the assessment such as AI, plagiarism and COVID
rules stay, and so do exam tables with their header row), removes admission
and study-right sentences, pointers to the admission rules and "Ingen utover
opptakskravet." from prerequisites, keeping a sentence that also names a
prerequisite (`.strip_admission_lines()`), drops
placeholder-only rows (`.placeholder_phrases`: "Ingen", "Se fagplanen.", "-",
Leganto pointers, "Oppgis senere.", "… ikke publisert ennå"), and drops a first
line that only repeats the section heading (but keeps learning-outcome group
labels such as "Kunnskap").

## What Each Mechanism May Remove

`course_plan_spec.md` says what the published text holds: personal data and
boilerplate are out of `course_plan` and the sections, other plan text stays
in `course_plan`, and a section holds only the plan text about its part. The
mechanisms that remove text run on different texts, so each may remove only
some of these:

| Mechanism | Code | Runs on | May remove |
|---|---|---|---|
| `selector` minus `exclude`; `.read_doc()` drops `script`, `style`, `noscript`, `select`, `label` | `R/institution_config.R`, `R/blocks.R`, `R/extract_fulltext.R` | `course_plan` and sections | personal data, boilerplate |
| `post_fn` (uit banner, year picker and contact block, which keeps the unit); `.cleanup_usn_text()` | `R/extract_fulltext.R` | `course_plan` (and usn's sections, cut from the text) | personal data, boilerplate |
| `anonymize_text()`: `.anon_*` handlers, then `.anon_generic()` | `R/anonymize.R` | `course_plan` and sections | personal data, boilerplate; a page that is not a plan (NA) |
| `facts` (title and facts box, and lists and stock text in no section, out of the id text); `normalize_plan_text()` | `R/institution_config.R`, `R/blocks.R`, `R/normalize_plan_text.R` | the plan id only | plan text that changes with the year, not with the plan |
| `.drop` headings, unmapped headings, text before the first heading | `R/section_heading_map.R`, `R/extract_sections.R` | sections only | plan text about no section |
| `.clean_sections()`: `.section_noise`, placeholders, admission lines | `R/extract_sections.R` | sections only | plan text about no section, placeholders |
| shell rule (`SHELL_MAX_NCHAR`) | `R/pipeline.R` | whether a page has a plan | pages that are not a plan |

So a rule that keeps plan text out of the sections belongs on the section side,
not in `exclude`, `post_fn` or `anonymize_text()`, which would take it out of
`course_plan` too. The spec's "Known deviations" lists the rules that do not
fit yet.

## Auditing a Pipeline Step

The `/audit-institutions <sections|fulltext|anonymization> [inst ...]` skill
(Claude Code) checks a pipeline step for every institution with one review
agent per institution. R scripts build a review packet per institution
(`R/audit/prepare_{check}.R`; for sections after the deterministic pre-pass
`R/audit/qa_sections.R`), the agents write findings to
`data/audit/{check}/findings/{inst}.json`, and `R/audit/aggregate.R` verifies
them (course ids and verbatim quotes must be in the packet) and writes a ranked
cross-institution report. Details: `.claude/skills/audit-institutions/SKILL.md`.

## Data Files: Published and Internal

Files that hold raw page text (`html`, `extracted_text`) contain staff names,
e-mail addresses and phone numbers and are never published. Everything that is
shared is built from the anonymized text (`anonymize_text()`). The data are
kept in one folder per stage, so the folder says what may be shared:

| Folder | Holds | Written by | In git |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/input/` | the DBH snapshots, the pipeline input | `data-raw/courses.R` | yes |
| `data/raw/` | the harvest, with personal data; append-only | harvesting only | no |
| `data/releases/{tag}/` | offerings, plans and sections of a finalized release | `finalize_release()` | no |
| `data/backup/` | earlier harvests kept but not read (personal data) | by hand | no |
| `data/interim/` | text rebuilt from the harvest, with personal data; never shared | `targets::tar_make()` | no |
| `data/processed/` | anonymized data or data without text; can be shared | `targets::tar_make()` | no |

`data/processed/` may only hold text that went through `anonymize_text()`. The
pipeline checks this on every build: target `privacy_check` scans the files for
e-mail addresses, phone numbers, "Name (Role)" lines and "Name, dekan"
signatures and warns, and `tests/testthat/test-anonymize.R` fails, on any hit.
The repository is public.

| File | Contents | Personal data | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/input/dbh_courses_{date}.parquet`, `dbh_programmes_{date}.parquet` | DBH tables 208 (courses) and 347 (programmes), the harvest input | none | in git |
| `data/raw/{inst}/{year}/{run}.parquet`, `data/raw/checkpoint/` | raw harvest: `html` (+ text and bytes of PDFs) | yes (raw) | internal |
| `data/raw/{inst}/ledger/{run}.parquet` | fetch ledger: URL, HTTP status, outcome and page hash per offering and run | none | internal |
| `data/variables.csv` | every variable of the published files, with its old name ("Variables") | none | in git; released with the data |
| `data/interim/plan_gaps.RDS` | course-years without a plan, reason, URLs tried | none | internal |
| `data/interim/extracted_text.RDS` | `extracted_text` rebuilt from the raw harvest | yes (raw) | internal |
| `data/interim/course_offerings_full.RDS` | offerings + `url`, `extracted_text`, `course_plan` | yes (`extracted_text`) | internal |
| `data/processed/course_offerings.RDS` | DBH metadata + `plan_content_id`, no text | none | published |
| `data/processed/course_plans.RDS` | anonymized `course_plan` (+ `course_plan_normalized`) | anonymized | published |
| `data/processed/plan_sections.RDS` | anonymized section `text` per plan | anonymized | publishable |
| `data/interim/teacher_ed/`, `data/processed/teacher_ed/` | the same files for the teacher-ed frame ("Frames") | as above | as above |
| `app/course_browser/data/browser_data.RDS` | course_browser payload: plans, offering metadata, sections | anonymized (no `extracted_text`) | internal (app) |
| `app/course_browser_ojs/data/*.parquet` | anonymized `course_plan` + slim offering metadata | anonymized | published with the OJS page (build artifact) |
| `data/audit/` | audit findings (quotes from anonymized text) | staff names redacted | in git |

The scan catches text that skipped the anonymizer, not names the anonymizer
misses; the anonymization audit (`/audit-institutions anonymization`) checks
that per institution.

## Data Structure

### Input Data (`data/input/dbh_*_{date}.parquet`)

The harvest's input is a dated snapshot of DBH, written by
`data-raw/courses.R` from DBH's bulk files: `dbh_courses_{date}.parquet` is
table 208 (Emner), every course of every institution, year and semester, all
levels and statuses, one row per course and semester;
`dbh_programmes_{date}.parquet` is table 347 (Studieprogram), with the
programmes' study type (`Studiumkode`). A new snapshot gets a new date and the
old ones stay. The snapshots keep DBH's column names. `dbh_courses()` reads the
latest (or the one of `date`), gives DBH's columns the pipeline's names
(`DBH_COLUMNS`; see "Variables") and adds `institution` and `course_code`:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
for (f in c("R/utils.R", "R/fetch_html_cols.R", "R/extract_fulltext.R", "R/institution_config.R")) source(f)
```

```{r}
courses <- dbh_courses("teacher_ed")
courses |> slice(1:2)
```

`dbh_courses()` is every course; `dbh_courses("teacher_ed")` keeps the
courses of the teacher education programmes (study types in
`TEACHER_ED_STUDIUM`, matched on institution and programme code: a programme
code is unique only within an institution). The teacher-ed frame is a filter of
the same snapshot, so its offerings have the same `course_id` in both.
`harvest_all()` without `courses` harvests every course; `tar_make()` builds
everything in `data/raw/` and writes the teacher-ed frame's files apart (see
"Frames").

Key columns:
- `institution`: Short code (e.g., "oslomet", "uia"); NA for an institution code no config has
- `course_code_raw`: DBH's course code (used in `course_id`)
- `course_code`: the code with the trailing version number removed (`canon_remove_trailing_num()`: "ABC123-1" → "ABC123")
- `year`, `semester_name` ("Vår", "Høst", "Sommer", "Vinter"; `canon_semester_name()` gives `course_id` spring, autumn, summer)
- `programme_code`, `programme_name`: the programme DBH registers the course under (one per row)
- `status`: course status (1 active, 2 new, 3 discontinued, 4 discontinued with active students). It is the last part of `course_id`, and a later snapshot can change it: an offering already in a raw file keeps the id it was first harvested under (`first_course_id()`)

DBH lists most courses under both semesters of a year, also when they are
taught in one. Where pages are semester-specific, about half the rows therefore
have no plan by design; see "Semester registration in DBH" in
`data/data_notes.qmd` before reading row-level success rates.

`harvest_institution()` returns the offerings with `course_id`, `url`, `html`,
`html_error`, `html_success` and `extracted_text` added, the rows of the raw
store ("Raw Store and Finalized Releases").

### Variables (`data/variables.csv`)

`data/variables.csv` documents every variable of the published files
(`course_offerings.RDS`, `course_plans.RDS`, `plan_sections.RDS`, of both
frames): the file, its name, type, source (the column of DBH table 208, or
how the pipeline gives it), meaning and codes, and `old_name`, its name in the
releases up to data-2026-10-16. `release_data()` hands it over with the data,
and `tests/testthat/test-dbh-input.R` checks it against the built files and
`DBH_COLUMNS`. `course_offerings_full.RDS` (internal) adds `url`,
`extracted_text`, `course_plan`, `course_plan_normalized` and `plan_nchar`.

Since 2026-10-16 the DBH columns have English snake_case names (methods.qmd,
"Variable names"); their values are DBH's (Norwegian names, DBH's codes), and
`year_from` and `year_to` are integers (double before). DBH's snapshots, the
raw files of the harvests until 2026-10-16 and the releases up to
data-2026-10-16 have DBH's names: the pipeline renames them where it reads such
data (`dbh_rename()`, in `dbh_courses()`, `read_raw()`, `read_checkpoint()`,
`frozen_changes()` and `release_data()`). Code that reads an old release can
rename it by the same pairs:

```{r}
#| eval: false
v <- read.csv("data/variables.csv")
pairs <- unique(v[v$old_name != v$variable, c("variable", "old_name")])
old <- readRDS("data/releases/data-2026-10-16/course_offerings.RDS") |>
  dplyr::rename(dplyr::any_of(setNames(pairs$old_name, pairs$variable)))
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
v <- read.csv("data/variables.csv")
knitr::kable(v)
```

## Institution-Specific Notes

**NORD.** The URL needs Norwegian characters in the semester parameter
(`HØST`/`VÅR`); ASCII `HOEST` falls back to a generic "Gjeldende
emnebeskrivelse" page without year-specific content. The site maps each
semester to its academic year (`VÅR&year=2023` gives the 2022/23 plan). For a
year it has no plan for, it shows the current plan, headed "Gjeldende
emnebeskrivelse (sist oppdatert 2026/27)"; `page_year` in the config reads that
year, and an offering whose page shows a later year gets no plan. Pattern:
`https://www.nord.no/studier/emner/{code}?year={year}&semester={HØST|VÅR}`.

**NTNU.** The URL has the year but not the semester. The year is the academic
year the page is for (`/2025` is "Studieår 2025/2026"), so a spring or summer
offering reads the year before (`url_year = "academic"`; HVL and OsloMet
likewise), and `read_harvest()` gives an offering the page at its URL
whichever offering it was fetched for. DBH's "-A" codes (MGLU1101-A) are the
site's code without the suffix. A page saying no
information is available raises `ntnu_no_info_error`. robots.txt asks for a
10-second crawl delay (`request_delay` in the config). The page's exam tab
(`#omEksamen`: assessment form, grading scale, exam sessions and their parts)
is read without its link, rooms, comments, dates and times; the assessment
section gets one session of it (`exam_sessions`). The timetable tab
(`#timeplan`, from 2025) is not read.

**UiO.** UiO publishes only the latest version of each course plan: the base
URL always returns the current plan and older versions cannot be reached.
Semester URLs (`/h24/`, `/v25/`) hold logistics only (teachers, timetable, exam
dates), not the plan, so they are not used. Data should be filtered to the
current year. The URL holds a faculty and department folder that DBH does
not give: `https://www.uio.no/studier/emner/{faculty}/{department}/{CODE}/`.
`resolve_urls_uio_batch()` reads the folders from UiO's sitemap
(`uio_course_folders()`), which lists every course taught now (the same
courses as the listing `/studier/emner/alle/`). A course not taught now keeps
its page but is not listed: it gets the folder that most listed courses with
its code prefix (`ENG`) have, else the one of its DBH department
(`department_code`); a wrong guess is a 404. A few folders are named in lower
case (`sv/iss/sos9009`), and the URL must be too; Ø is O (`MØNA2504` is in
`hf/ikos/MONA2504/`).

**HiOF.** Courses before autumn 2021 use a different URL structure (switch in
`add_course_url_hiof()`); the config selector lists fallbacks for the old and
new page layouts.

**USN.** The URL holds a version number that metadata cannot give:
`https://www.usn.no/studier/studie-og-emneplaner/#/emne/{CODE}_{VERSION}_{YEAR}_{SEMESTER}`.
Each version (1, 2, 3, …) is a revision valid for a range of years, and an
invalid version/year combination silently shows another page without changing
the URL. `resolve_urls_usn_batch()` therefore renders each candidate in Chrome
(`rvest::read_html_live()`, hash routing) and checks that the displayed
"Undervisningsstart" year matches. It tries versions 1-3 and stops early when
the course code is missing from the page (no such version) or version 1 starts
after the requested year (course did not exist yet); NA means no version exists
for that semester. The content is rendered inside Shadow DOM, which
`html_text()` cannot read; `read_usn_live_html(session)` walks the shadow roots
with JavaScript:

```{r}
#| eval: false
session <- rvest::read_html_live(url)
Sys.sleep(5)  # wait for JS rendering
content <- read_usn_live_html(session)
session$session$close()
```

The batch resolver reuses one Chrome session and navigates by changing
`window.location.hash`, which avoids a 2-3 s browser start per URL. A
semester without a plan of its own shows another semester's plan under the
banner "Emneplanen for dette semesteret er ikke klar ennå". When the next
candidate shows the same plan, the banner stays until the page is reloaded, so
a page with the requested year and the banner is reloaded. HTML is
captured during resolution, so USN has no separate fetch step.

**UiT.** Historical plans need a document id:
`https://uit.no/utdanning/emner/emne?p_document_id={ID}`. The active page
(`/utdanning/aktivt/emne/{CODE}`) has a `<select>` listing every semester with
its document id (option text `{CODE}: H 2020` / `{CODE}: V 2021`), also for
discontinued courses. A semester listed twice can be an English document
("Course code:") beside the Norwegian one; `uit_one_per_semester()` fetches
those and keeps the first Norwegian one. The same CSS selector works for
active and historical pages.

**Samas.** `noop` strategy: `extracted_text` is NA, since the plans are in Sámi.

## Key Functions Reference

| Function | File | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `harvest_institution(institution, courses, year, refetch)` | `R/harvest.R` | Harvest one institution with its configured strategy |
| `harvest_all(courses, year, refetch, institutions, retry)` | `R/harvest.R` | Harvest all (or the given) institutions; each harvest adds a run, `data/raw/{inst}/{year}/{date}.parquet` |
| `write_raw_run(rows, institution, run)`, `read_raw(files)` | `R/utils.R` | Write a harvest run to the raw store; read raw files in harvest order |
| `fetch_ledger(rows, institution, run)`, `raw_ledger(files)` | `R/utils.R` | A run's fetch ledger; the ledger of raw files, recorded or reconstructed (target `ledger`) |
| `fetch_outcome(url, page, status, error)`, `offering_outcome(course_id, url, ledger)` | `R/utils.R` | Outcome class of a fetch; how an offering's URL answered last (retries) |
| `site_request(url)` | `R/fetch_html_cols.R` | A request to a course site: user agent, timeout, retries of timeouts and server errors |
| `fetch_coverage(frame, ledger, offerings)`, `page_changes(ledger, files, config)` | `R/pipeline.R` | Fetch outcome, plan and retry of every offering of a frame; pages changed between runs (targets `coverage`, `changed_pages`) |
| `raw_partitions()`, `read_raw(files, content = FALSE)`, `raw_page_id(file, row)` | `R/utils.R` | The raw store's institution x year partitions; raw rows with the page id in place of the page |
| `partition_blocks()`, `partition_text()`, `partition_sections()` | `R/pipeline.R` | Per raw partition: every page's blocks, text and plan (`page_plans()`), and the sections of the pages plans are cut from |
| `plan_offerings(pages, page_text, config)` | `R/pipeline.R` | Every offering with the text, `course_plan` and plan id of its page (target `courses`) |
| `frame_members()`, `frame_plans()`, `frame_sections()`, `frame_offerings()`, `frame_dir()` | `R/pipeline.R`, `R/utils.R` | The frames: their offerings, plans (`plan_table()`), sections and data folders |
| `harvest_files(institution)`, `harvested_institutions()` | `R/utils.R` | An institution's raw files, run by run; the institutions with raw files |
| `dbh_courses(frame, date)` | `R/utils.R` | DBH offerings of a snapshot: all courses, or the teacher-ed frame (`"teacher_ed"`) |
| `dbh_rename(df)` | `R/utils.R` | DBH's column names (snapshots, raw files and releases until 2026-10-16) as the pipeline's (`DBH_COLUMNS`) |
| `institution_from_code(code)` | `R/institution_config.R` | Institution short name for DBH institution codes |
| `get_institution_config(inst)` | `R/institution_config.R` | Config list for one institution |
| `add_course_id(dbh_df)` | `R/utils.R` | Unique id from institution, raw code, year, semester, status |
| `add_course_url(df)` | `R/add_course_url.R` | Institution-specific URL builders; NA where discovery is needed |
| `resolve_course_urls(df, checkpoint_path)` | `R/resolve_course_urls.R` | URL discovery (USN, UiT, hivolda, UiO) with checkpointing |
| `fetch_html_with_checkpoint(courses, checkpoint_path)` | `R/checkpoint.R` | Download HTML, skipping courses already in the checkpoint |
| `extract_fulltext_from_raw(df, config)` | `R/extract_fulltext.R` | `extracted_text` from the raw harvest, per strategy |
| `page_blocks(html, text, cfg)` | `R/blocks.R` | Read one page into a block table |
| `page_fulltext(blocks, config)` | `R/extract_fulltext.R` | A page's `extracted_text` from its blocks |
| `read_harvest(files, config, content)` | `R/pipeline.R` | One institution's raw files combined (`harvest_files()`): the page each offering takes; current sites matched by course code and academic year |
| `harvested_rows(institutions)` | `R/pipeline.R` | `read_harvest()` joined with `data/interim/extracted_text.RDS` (audit scripts) |
| `finalize_release(tag)`, `frozen_changes()` | `R/release.R` | Lock a release's raw files; list changes to it (target `frozen_check`) |
| `release_data(tag, dest, frame)` | `R/release.R` | Copy the published files of a frame (the teacher-ed one), `methods.md`, `data/variables.csv`, a manifest and section coverage to the coding project |
| `plan_gaps(offerings, fetch_status)` | `R/pipeline.R` | Course-years without a plan, with the reason (target `gaps`) |
| `validate_courses(df, stage)` | `R/utils.R` | Required columns at `"initial"`, `"with_url"`, `"with_html"` |
| `anonymize_text(institution, text)` | `R/anonymize.R` | PII and admin-date removal for `course_plan` and sections |
| `normalize_plan_text(course_plan)` | `R/normalize_plan_text.R` | Lossy normalization for dedup hashing |
| `plan_ids(id_text)`, `plan_table(courses)`, `deduplicate_plans(df)` | `R/deduplicate_plans.R` | Content hashes (`plan_content_id`); the unique plans of a set of offerings |
| `page_sections(blocks, text, cfg)` | `R/extract_sections.R` | A page's sections from its blocks |
| `extract_sections(config, html, extracted_text, course_id)` | `R/extract_sections.R` | `page_sections()` for many pages |

## Troubleshooting

**URLs look wrong?**
- Check the institution's builder in `R/add_course_url.R`
- Print a few: `courses |> filter(institution == "inst") |> add_course_url() |> select(url) |> head()`

**HTML download fails?**
- Check if the website is accessible in a browser
- Count the outcomes: `raw_ledger(harvest_files("inst")) |> dplyr::count(outcome, http_status)`
- Look at `html_error` for error messages
- Some institutions rate-limit or block automated requests
- For NTNU, check whether the page says no information is available

**Extracted text is empty or wrong?**
- Verify the CSS selector with browser dev tools on a real course page
- Update the selector in `R/institution_config.R` if the website changed, then `targets::tar_make()` (no new harvest needed)
- Read one page into blocks and look at them: `page_blocks(html, NA, .block_cfg(get_institution_config("inst")))`
- Some pages have different structures for different years

**Content missing from JavaScript-rendered pages?**
- Shadow DOM content is invisible to `html_text()`; see USN above
- `session$session$Runtime$evaluate("...")` runs JavaScript in a live session
- `session$view()` opens the browser to see what is rendered

**"the site refuses the harvest (HTTP 429 ...)"?**
- The site answered 403 or 429, so its harvest stopped; the pages fetched so
  far are in the checkpoint. Harvest it again later (the checkpoint resumes),
  at night, or with a longer `request_delay` in `R/institution_config.R`

**Checkpoint file is huge?**
- This is normal - HTML is large
- Checkpoint files are in `.gitignore`; deleting one makes the next run fetch again
  the offerings that are not yet in a raw file (never the ones that are)

**"raw files are not written twice"?**
- A run of that name exists: two harvests of the same institution in the same
  second, or a run written by hand. The raw store is append-only; run the
  harvest again

**"offerings in more than one raw file"?**
- Two runs of an institution hold the same `course_id` (not a retry); a file
  was copied into `data/raw/` by hand. Remove the copy

## File Organization

```
├── _targets.R                 # Post-harvest pipeline: targets::tar_make()
├── methods.qmd                # Methods choices for articles (rendered to methods.md)
├── course_plan_spec.md        # What course_plan and the sections hold, and what stays out
├── renv.lock                  # Pinned package versions (renv::restore())
├── .github/workflows/tests.yml # Tests on GitHub Actions
├── R/
│   ├── harvest.R              # Entry points: harvest_institution(), harvest_all()
│   ├── harvest_strategies.R   # Strategy implementations
│   ├── institution_config.R   # Institution registry (strategy, selectors, overrides, section_*)
│   ├── utils.R                # Helpers (data paths, add_course_id, validation, normalization)
│   ├── add_course_url.R       # URL generation logic
│   ├── resolve_course_urls.R  # URL discovery for USN, UiT, hivolda, UiO
│   ├── fetch_html_cols.R      # HTML downloading (httr2)
│   ├── extract_fulltext.R     # Config-driven text extraction
│   ├── checkpoint.R           # Checkpoint management
│   ├── anonymize.R            # PII removal: anonymize_text() for course_plan and sections
│   ├── normalize_plan_text.R  # Lossy normalization for dedup hashing
│   ├── deduplicate_plans.R    # Groups identical plans by content hash
│   ├── section_heading_map.R  # Heading → section patterns (incl. ".drop")
│   ├── extract_sections.R     # Section extraction strategies + cleanup
│   ├── pipeline.R             # Steps of the {targets} pipeline (_targets.R)
│   ├── pipeline_metrics.R     # Regression snapshot: check_pipeline_metrics()
│   ├── release.R              # release_data(), finalize_release(), frozen_changes()
│   └── audit/                # Audit harness for /audit-institutions
├── app/
│   ├── course_browser/        # Shiny concordance browser; build_data.R → data/ (see its README)
│   └── course_browser_ojs/    # Static Observable JS browser; build_data.R → data/ (see its README)
├── data/                      # README "Data Files: Published and Internal"
│   ├── input/                 # DBH snapshots dbh_{courses,programmes}_{date}.parquet (in git)
│   ├── raw/                   # Harvest: {inst}/{year}/{run}.parquet, {inst}/ledger/, checkpoint/ (not in git)
│   ├── interim/               # Rebuilt text with personal data (not in git); teacher_ed/: that frame's
│   ├── processed/             # Anonymized data files, can be shared (not in git); teacher_ed/: that frame's
│   ├── releases/              # Finalized releases' data (not in git)
│   ├── backup/                # Earlier harvests, not read (not in git)
│   ├── audit/                 # Audit findings and reports
│   ├── variables.csv          # Every variable of the data files, old and new names
│   └── data_notes.qmd         # Data quality notes per institution
├── tests/
│   ├── testthat/              # Rscript -e 'testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat")'
│   └── snapshots/             # pipeline_metrics_{frame}.csv; raw_manifest.csv once a release is finalized
└── data-raw/
    ├── courses.R              # script that writes a DBH snapshot to data/input/
    └── raw_to_parquet.R       # the one-time conversion of the RDS raw files (2026-10-16)
```
